title: Senior Director, Enterprise Compliance
description: Hi, we're Oscar. We're hiring a Senior Director, Enterprise Compliance to join our Compliance team. Oscar is the first health insurance company built around a full stack technology platform and a relentless focus on serving our members. We started Oscar in 2012 to create the kind of health insurance company we would want for ourselves—one that behaves like a doctor in the family. About the role: The Senior Director, Enterprise Compliance supports the execution and continuous improvement of Oscar's enterprise compliance program. Reporting to the Chief Compliance Officer, you will provide leadership over key compliance functions, including regulatory compliance, regulatory change management/implementation, compliance operations, investigations, monitoring and auditing, policy governance, and compliance education. You will anticipate regulatory and industry developments, translates them into enterprise compliance priorities, and partners with cross-functional leaders to identify and mitigate compliance risks, strengthen internal controls, and promote a culture of ethics and integrity. You will exercise significant independent judgment, develops a compliance organization, and serves as a trusted advisor to business leaders on complex healthcare regulatory matters. You will report into the Vice President, Chief Compliance Officer. Work Location: This position is based in our New York City office, requiring a hybrid work schedule with 3 days of in-office work per week. Thursdays are a required in-office day for team meetings and events, while your other two office days are flexible to suit your schedule. #LI-Hybrid Pay Transparency: The base pay for this role is: $218,592 - $286,902 per year. You are also eligible for employee benefits, participation in Oscar's unlimited vacation program, company equity grants and annual performance bonuses. Responsibilities: Lead the execution and continuous improvement of Oscar's enterprise compliance program, including the multi-year compliance strategy, annual compliance work plans, risk assessments, policy governance, regulatory change management/implementation, monitoring, auditing, and reporting activities. Translate enterprise compliance priorities into an relevant operating plan; establish ownership and governance; allocate resources; develop compliance managers and team members; remove barriers; and lead accountability for measurable outcomes. Anticipate regulatory and industry developments and advise senior leaders on their possible effects for Oscar's products, market participation, business strategy, and operating model. Provide guidance on federal and state healthcare regulations, contractual obligations, and emerging regulatory risks across applicable lines of business. Oversee compliance investigations, hotline reporting, the Special Investigations Unit, fraud-prevention activities, corrective action plans, and remediation efforts, ensuring timely resolution and appropriate escalation of significant compliance concerns. Partner with leaders across Legal, Privacy, Security, Internal Audit, Enterprise Risk, Clinical, Product, Operations, and People teams to embed compliance requirements into business processes and strategic initiatives. Set and uphold enterprise standards for ethics and compliance by leading education, communications, and awareness initiatives that strengthen Oscar's culture of ethics and compliance. Lead compliance reporting and engagement for executive leadership, Compliance Committee, Board committees, and regulatory examinations; support interactions with regulators and external auditors. Compliance with all applicable laws and regulations Other duties as assigned Requirements: 12+ years of progressively responsible experience in healthcare compliance, regulatory affairs, legal compliance, audit, or enterprise risk management. 5+ years leading high-performing compliance teams and enterprise-wide compliance initiatives. Demonstrated experience designing, implementing, and maintaining an effective healthcare compliance program aligned with OIG Compliance Program Guidance and applicable federal and state regulations. Experience supporting highly regulated healthcare organizations, including health plans, managed care organizations, healthcare technology companies, provider organizations, or related entities. Track record of anticipating regulatory developments and translating them into enterprise priorities, operating plans, and business controls. Demonstrated experience leading complex compliance investigations, monitoring and auditing activities, regulatory risk assessments, corrective action planning, and policy governance. Experience advising senior business leaders on complex regulatory and operational compliance issues and leading their resolution Strong written and verbal communication skills, experience presenting to executive leadership, governance committees, regulators, or external auditors. title: Senior Risk Officer
description: Blockchain is connecting the world to the future of finance. As the most trusted and fastest-growing global crypto company, it helps millions of people worldwide safely access cryptocurrency. Since its inception in 2011, Blockchain has earned the trust of over 90 million wallet holders and more than 40 million verified users, facilitating over $1 trillion in crypto transactions. We’re looking for a Senior Risk Officer to help build and run risk management across Blockchain.com. This is a company-wide role: you'll help identify, measure, and manage risk across our business lines, working closely with Compliance, Legal, Finance, Product, and Operations to strengthen our overall risk posture as we continue to scale and expand our business. A key part of this role is supporting our expansion into regulated derivatives. Blockchain.com already offers millions of customers a trusted way to buy, sell, and hold crypto, and we're extending those offerings into regulated futures and derivatives markets in the U.S. and other jurisdictions. You'll help build out the risk management program for that and other regulated derivatives entities, working alongside their compliance and risk officers to make sure risk is identified, monitored, and escalated appropriately as the business grows. You'll report into our broader Risk function and partner with senior leadership across the company to shape how we manage risk—from market, credit, and liquidity risk to operational, technology, and counterparty risk—while bringing specialized attention to the unique risks of our regulated derivatives activities. If you've built or run risk programs at a financial institution and want to apply that experience across a global crypto platform, this is the perfect opportunity for you. WHAT YOU WILL DO Help design, implement, and administer risk management frameworks, policies, and controls across the company's business lines Identify, measure, monitor, and report on key risk categories, including market, credit, liquidity, operational, technology, legal, and counterparty risk Establish and maintain risk tolerance limits, monitor for breaches, and escalate issues to senior management and governance committees as needed Support the risk management program for the firm's regulated derivatives entities, covering areas such as customer fund segregation, margin and collateral adequacy, capital risk, and settlement risk Partner with the business’s compliance function and regulatory counsel to ensure risk controls meet applicable regulatory expectations across the jurisdictions in which the firm operates Help oversee risk related to digital asset collateral, including valuation, haircuts, custody arrangements, and liquidation triggers Prepare and deliver regular risk exposure reporting to senior management, risk committees, and, where applicable, regulators and self-regulatory organizations Partner with Product and Engineering to assess and manage risk as new products and features are launched Support business continuity, disaster recovery, and operational resilience planning Contribute to the annual review and testing of risk management programs and controls, and help track remediation of identified gaps Advise senior leadership on emerging risks as the business and its product offerings evolve, including in fast-moving areas like crypto derivatives WHAT YOU WILL NEED 8+ years of risk management experience at a financial institution, broker-dealer, futures firm, exchange, or similar regulated entity Strong working knowledge of core risk disciplines—market, credit, liquidity, and operational risk—and how they apply in practice Experience building, implementing, or enhancing a risk management program or framework Excellent judgment and the confidence to make sound risk calls in a fast-moving, evolving business Clear, plain-English communication skills–you can explain risk concepts to engineers, executives, and regulators alike Comfort working across a wide range of stakeholders and business lines in a company supporting multiple regulated activities NICE TO HAVE Experience with futures, derivatives, or FCM risk management, including customer fund segregation, margin, and collateral risk Experience supporting a new regulated entity through registration, licensing, or similar regulatory processes Familiarity with crypto or digital asset products and their associated risks Experience with enterprise risk management programs spanning multiple business lines or entities Familiarity with risk considerations across multiple regulatory regimes and jurisdictions COMPENSATIONS & PERKS Unlimited vacation policy; work hard and take time when you need it. Unlimited books policy; order the technical resources you need or simply pick something up from our company library. Apple equipment. Full-time salary based on experience and meaningful equity in an industry-leading company. Role based in our Malta office, with a mandatory in-office presence four days per wee

title: Lead BRC Risk Advisor
description: Location: 127 Public Square, Cleveland Ohio Location: Cleveland, OH or Buffalo NY preferred. Hybrid Requirement (if within specific cities): Selected candidate resides in Key Bank footprint are expected to work on-site 3 days per week at the nearest KeyBank office (non-branch location). Remote Option: If the selected candidate lives outside of KeyBank’s geographic footprint, the position will be considered fully remote. Job Summary The Lead BRC Risk Advisor is a first-line risk partner embedded within the Commercial Bank, supporting business leaders and peers across Commercial Banking. The role helps identify, assess, and manage risk; strengthen the control environment; and translate enterprise risk requirements into practical solutions for Commercial Bank processes, products, and client activities. The advisor leads and project manages cross-functional risk efforts, including issues and remediation, control design and enhancement, risk assessments, regulatory and audit support, and stakeholder reporting. The role coordinates business, 1LOD, 2LOD, and other partners to drive timely decisions, clear accountability, sustainable remediation, and transparent updates to leadership. Essential Functions Serve as a trusted first-line risk advisor to Commercial Bank leaders and peers, providing practical guidance on risk, controls, governance, and enterprise risk requirements. Lead and project manage issues and remediation from identification through closure, including root-cause analysis, remediation-plan development, milestones, stakeholder coordination, status reporting, escalation, and closure documentation. Draft new controls and review or enhance existing controls in accordance with RCSA and enterprise risk standards, partnering with business owners to ensure controls are practical, sustainable, and appropriately mitigate risk. Support Commercial Bank RCSA and risk-profile activities, including risk and control assessments, testing results, residual risk, risk metrics, emerging risks, and executive-level reporting. Coordinate cross-functional risk initiatives across Commercial Bank businesses, bringing together business, operations, product, 1LOD, 2LOD, Compliance, Legal, Audit, and other partners as appropriate. Provide regular, concise updates to business and risk stakeholders on project status, risks, decisions, dependencies, remediation progress, and items requiring escalation. Lead or support risk activities associated with business and process changes, products and services, regulatory requirements, and other Commercial Bank initiatives; track timelines and deliverables to keep work on schedule. Support internal audits, regulatory examinations, and second-line reviews by coordinating information requests, business responses, remediation, and follow-up activities. Monitor findings, control performance, risk metrics, and trends to identify emerging concerns and opportunities to strengthen the Commercial Bank control environment. Build strong relationships across the Commercial Bank and enterprise risk functions, helping peers navigate risk processes and promoting consistent, accountable risk management. Mentor teammates and share risk-management knowledge, tools, and practices across the team. Perform other duties as assigned and comply with all KeyBank policies, procedures, and standards of professional and ethical conduct. Education Bachelor's Degree (preferred) OR equivalent experience (required) Work Experience 3+ years of relevant experience in risk management, controls, compliance, audit, project management, or Commercial Banking (required) Skills Strong knowledge of first-line risk management and the Commercial Bank environment, including lending, deposits, payments, servicing, products, and related operational processes. Demonstrated ability to lead issues management and remediation efforts, organize complex work, manage milestones and dependencies, and drive work through completion. Strong control-design and risk-assessment capabilities, including RCSA, risk identification, control evaluation, testing results, residual risk, and risk metrics. Effective project-management skills with the ability to coordinate multiple stakeholders and workstreams, establish accountability, manage timelines, and escalate barriers appropriately. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex risk topics into clear recommendations and concise updates for business leaders and risk partners. Ability to build trusted partnerships across business, 1LOD, 2LOD, Compliance, Legal, Audit, Operations, Product, and Technology teams. Strong analytical judgment and attention to detail, with the ability to identify trends, evaluate risk implications, and recommend practical, sustainable solutions. Ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic Commercial Bank environment while maintaining high standards of accuracy and execution. Working knowledge of regulatory, audit, and compliance

The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.”  learn more about working at Coinbase . As a Group Product Manager on the AI Foundations team within the Platform product group, you'll own the product strategy and roadmap for the core AI building blocks that every team at Coinbase depends on. This team owns the LLM Gateway, model selection, MCPs, knowledge and context primitives, evaluations, and additional AI infrastructure that powers autonomous and assisted AI experiences across the company. You'll define how Coinbase builds, governs, and scales its AI capabilities, turning foundational primitives into reliable, secure, and high-leverage tools that accelerate product development and operational efficiency company-wide. What you’ll do: Shape the multi-year vision for AI platform capabilities, identifying emerging technologies and industry shifts that inform investment priorities and architectural decisions. Own the end-to-end product roadmap and success metrics for AI Foundations, spanning model infrastructure, context and knowledge primitives, integration frameworks, and evaluation systems. Drive adoption of AI primitives across Coinbase product and engineering teams by building self-serve capabilities, clear documentation, and compelling internal developer experiences. Lead model governance strategy, defining how Coinbase evaluates, integrates, and manages large language models across cost, quality, latency, and safety dimensions. Partner with Engineering, Security, Legal, and Finance to ensure AI infrastructure meets Coinbase's standards for reliability, compliance, and responsible use. Required Skills and Experience:   10+ years of product management experience, with 5+ years focused on AI/ML platforms, developer tools, or infrastructure products used by internal engineering teams. Proven track record of defining and shipping platform primitives or developer-facing products that achieved broad internal or external adoption. Deep technical fluency in LLM architectures, model serving, prompt engineering, evaluation frameworks, and agent-based systems, with the ability to engage directly with engineers on design tradeoffs. Demonstrated ability to lead complex, cross-functional initiatives across engineering, security, legal, and finance in a fast-moving, regulated environment. Builds conviction with senior and executive stakeholders around ambiguous, high-stakes platform bets, articulating complex technical strategy, investment cases, and tradeoffs in clear narratives that drive alignment and resource decisions. Review fund expenses and accruals and compare them to annual budgets to identify outliers and propose adjustments as necessary. Together with our members, we’re changing the way people think about and interact with personal finance. We’re a next-generation financial services company and national bank using innovative, mobile-first technology to help our millions of members reach their goals. The industry is going through an unprecedented transformation, and we’re at the forefront. We’re proud to come to work every day knowing that what we do has a direct impact on people’s lives, with our core values guiding us every step of the way. Join us to invest in yourself, your career, and the financial world. The role: SoFi is seeking an energetic, detail-oriented, self-motivated, and intellectually curious Independent Risk Management (IRM) Director to support the growth of our Invest business.  Your success in this role will rely on deep subject matter expertise in broker-dealer, investment advisory matters, and retail investment product risks. This person will serve as the senior second-line risk leader responsible for independent risk oversight of the Invest business. This role will act as the primary risk partner to Invest leadership, providing credible challenge, strategic risk advisory, and oversight across all material risk categories associated with the business, excluding Compliance Risk, which is overseen by a dedicated Invest Compliance organization. We offer the excitement of a rapidly growing startup with the stability of an industry leading leadership team. Become a trusted advisor to senior business leaders on risk implications of strategic decisions, product expansion, operational changes, and emerging risks. Support post-launch reviews and continuous control enhancements as the business scales. title: Investment Governance Manager

By delivering the combined power of our distinctive investment management capabilities, we provide a wide range of investment strategies and vehicles to our clients around the world. If you're looking for challenging work, intelligent colleagues, and exposure across a global footprint, come explore your potential at Invesco. What’s in it for you? Our people are at the ver y core of our success. Invesco employees get more out of life through our comprehensive compensation and benefit offerings including: Flexible paid time off Hybrid work schedule 401(K) matching of 100% up to the first 6% with a discretionary supplemental contribution Health & wellbeing benefits Parental Leave benefits Employee stock purchase plan Job Description About the Team The Investment Governance team is responsible for the first-line governance framework that provides for oversight of the investment lifecycle, operating standards, incident management and effective risk mitigation across Invesco’s global investment platform. The team partners with Investments, Capital Markets, Front Office Operations and LCAR functions to strengthen first-line processes, improve decision-making, ensure appropriate escalation, reporting and oversight. About the Role The role supports the design, implementation and ongoing operation of Invesco’s global investment governance framework. This includes the development of robust governance documentation and decision-useful management information, advising governance bodies on potential enhancements to ensure appropriate oversight of risks, coordinating investment incident management and reporting processes, analyzing investment lifecycle events and developing operational playbooks to mitigate risk. Working across Investments, Capital Markets, Front Office Operations and the three lines of defense, the role promotes a multi-layered investment governance approach in support of the delivery of good client outcomes. The position reports to the Global Head of Investment Governance. Responsibilities of the Role Provide first-line ownership of investment-related policies, standards, procedures, and guidance. Coordinate the intake, assessment, triage, escalation, and governance of investment and trading incidents. Ensure consistency of incident records to support better management information and reporting. Track incident remediation plans, accountable owners, and deadlines, and support the delivery of remediation plans within the first line. Map investment lifecycle activities and material risks across relevant asset classes and develop playbooks and checklists to support effective risk management and improved decision-making. Produce management information, dashboards, and committee reporting on a variety of governance topics. Coordinate engagement with Legal, Compliance, Audit, Risk and Controls Assurance on governance topics and investment process enhancements. Support the Global Head of Investment Governance on the execution of investment governance initiatives arising out of the design and implementation of Invesco’s global investment governance framework. Requirements for the Role Bachelor’s degree in finance, economics, accounting, business, risk management, law or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience. Typically, five or more years of relevant experience in asset management, investment operations, investment risk, operational risk, governance and controls, compliance, internal audit or front-office business management. Strong knowledge of the investment lifecycle, including portfolio management, order generation, trading, post-trade activities, investment data and support processes. Experience drafting and maintaining investment, trading, risk or control policies and procedures and supporting audit, assurance or governance reviews. Strong organizational, analytical and communication skills, with experience producing clear papers, management information, dashboards and senior-management reporting. Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word. Familiarity with investment data, order management systems, operational resilience or regulatory change is advantageous. Relevant professional qualification, or progress towards one, such as CFA, FRM, CAIA, CIA, CPA, CISA or an equivalent credential, is preferred. title: Legal Program Manager
description: About the Team OpenAI’s Legal team helps advance our mission by tackling novel legal issues in AI. Our team brings together professionals across technology, privacy, intellectual property, corporate, employment, tax, regulatory, and litigation. Our regulatory compliance work turns legal requirements into practical programs that support responsible AI development and deployment. About the Role As a Legal Program Manager, you will independently manage assigned programs and workstreams across Legal priorities, with a focus on emerging user risk. Your portfolio may include sensitive user escalations, intake and response workflows, and improvements informed by recurring issues, with the mix evolving alongside team needs. You will partner with counsel, senior legal program managers, and technical and business teams to establish priorities and scope, then drive day-to-day execution. You’ll organize information, coordinate partners, and move open questions toward decisions. As you develop expertise, you’ll take on more ambiguous projects and build repeatable processes that help teams work more effectively. This full-time role is based in San Francisco, CA, or New York, NY. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you will: - Independently manage assigned legal programs and workstreams: define plans, owners, milestones, and dependencies within agreed scope, anticipate blockers, and drive execution. - Translate counsel’s and specialist teams’ guidance into repeatable workflows, playbooks, and documentation. Depending on your portfolio, this may include intake, sensitive user escalations, information gathering, and response coordination. - Build strong partnerships across Legal, Product, Safety, User Operations, Policy, and other teams to clarify ownership, coordinate handoffs, and drive commitments through completion. - Clarify open questions, gather and verify information, synthesize partner input, and bring recommendations and tradeoffs to the appropriate decision-makers. Escalate decisions that require changes to priorities, scope, or resources. - Maintain a reliable source of truth for matters, source documents, owners, deadlines, decisions, and actions. Provide concise reporting on progress, blockers, and decisions needed. - Identify recurring issues and execution gaps, propose practical improvements, and lead agreed changes through implementation and adoption. Use tools and automation thoughtfully, verify outputs, and assess improvements in quality, timeliness, and partner effort. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have demonstrated experience independently managing programs or projects from planning through delivery in legal operations, business operations, compliance, policy, investigations, or a related field. - Have experience coordinating work across teams, maintaining reliable records, and driving open questions and actions to resolution. Experience working with an in-house legal team or in a technology environment is a plus. - Have improved a recurring workflow, documented the change, and helped others adopt it. You can explain what improved and how you assessed the result. - Take ownership of execution, set and achieve milestones, anticipate dependencies, and follow through without frequent direction. - Bring strong organizational, analytical, and communication skills. Exercise sound judgment under pressure, adapt to changing priorities, and know when to proceed independently or seek guidance. - Handle sensitive information and difficult subject matter with discretion and care, distinguish evidence from assumptions, and recognize when counsel or specialist input is needed. - Are resourceful and hands-on, with enthusiasm for AI technology and the ability to learn unfamiliar subject areas, use AI tools thoughtfully, and verify their outputs. - Bring familiarity with user safety, legal escalations, preservation, incident response, or operational data as a plus.
